PullRequest.Title: Restore API proposal registry safeguard in official builds
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Restore the API proposal registry safeguard in the active production `core-ci` path. The legacy production compile regenerated this file; this change intentionally uses **read-only validation** instead, failing with an explicit update command rather than silently repairing tracked sources. The current registry is already consistent and is not changed by this PR.

- Share the existing registry generation and source-discovery logic between validation and developer regeneration, preserving metadata, ordering, formatting, and LF/CRLF handling.
- Await `check-api-proposal-names` as the first `core-ci` task, before compilation, transpilation, and bundling. Existing production, quality, and PR CI callers inherit it without duplicate builds or YAML changes.
- Keep `compile-api-proposal-names`, developer compilation, build-fast, and watch regeneration intact; document both commands.
- Add focused regression coverage for additions/removals/renames, stale or missing output, unreadable inputs, newline handling, actionable errors, no writes, and actual task sequencing.

## Validation

- `node --test build/lib/test/apiProposalNames.test.ts build/next/test/build-fast.test.ts` — **38 passed**.
- `npm run gulp check-api-proposal-names` — real registry passes without changes.
- Actual `core-ci` CLI on an isolated stale fixture — exit **1**, actionable update command, no consumers started, and fixture unchanged.
- Targeted ESLint, staged-file hygiene, scoped build-tool dependency-graph typecheck, and `git diff --check` passed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Production and PR `core-ci` build with an up-to-date API proposal registry
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The added `check-api-proposal-names` task must finish before extension packaging, TypeScript type-checking, transpilation, and bundling can start. Its synchronous scan and reads are therefore on the build critical path; downstream work is unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the declarations directory and synchronously glob the complete `src/vscode-dts/**` tree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One recursive traversal per `core-ci` run over roughly 135 proposal files and a small number of other entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The active `core-ci` path did not validate or scan proposal declarations before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Introduced as the first serial build step, so this bounded traversal must complete before any existing build consumer starts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronously read every matched proposal declaration to verify readability, then read the generated registry once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full read per effective proposal file (roughly 135 today), plus one registry read, all serial.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The active `core-ci` path performed none of these validation reads. Legacy/developer generation scanned this corpus on different build paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Introduced on the front of the build critical path; the bytes read scale with declaration corpus size but remain a single bounded repository-local pass.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Package marketplace/local extensions and extension media through gulp streams.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Repository extension/media corpus once per build, with existing grouping in the packaging streams.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same extension packaging stages were already in `core-ci` in the same order.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing serial stages still run after the new check; the diff neither increases their cardinality nor changes their implementation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run one native TypeScript type-check subprocess, one esbuild transpile subprocess, then three esbuild bundle subprocesses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Five subprocesses per build: type-check and transpile serially, followed by three concurrent target bundles.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same subprocesses and sequencing existed before the diff, without the proposal validation preceding them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All are existing downstream critical-path work and now start only after the validation pass; their own count and concurrency are unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One `src/vscode-dts` tree containing roughly 135 registered proposals (the generated registry ends at line 551), plus a small number of non-proposal entries. Work scales linearly with proposal count and declaration bytes, once per `core-ci` invocation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The new readdir/glob and declaration/registry reads execute synchronously and serially in one Node process. `task.series` then preserves the existing downstream ordering; after transpilation, the three esbuild bundle subprocesses still run in parallel. In the quality pipeline, other npm-run-all jobs remain separate concurrent processes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no application cache or coalescing because the check runs once per build. Cold runs incur filesystem metadata and file reads; warm runs benefit only from the OS page cache. Success and failure both stop after this single scan, with stale registries failing before downstream work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the synchronous filesystem pass is newly on the critical path and scales linearly with proposals; line-level task composition and filesystem calls prove it. Confidence is also high that it occurs only once and does not multiply downstream boundaries.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact declaration byte volume and elapsed time on each CI filesystem were not measured. The repository establishes a bounded corpus of about 135 proposals and only one pass per build; this is small relative to the existing full extension packaging, type-check, transpile, and three bundles.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR intentionally adds a bounded, fail-fast validation pass to a full production build. Although it adds serial filesystem work, realistic cardinality is modest, execution is once per build, and there is no evidence of material latency compared with the existing full compile/bundle path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Developer explicit compilation and watch regeneration of the API proposal registry
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For explicit compilation, gulp must scan the proposal source glob, the generator must flush, and any changed registry write must finish. In watch mode the same regeneration runs after the existing 200 ms watcher delay and debounce; unrelated type-check/watch tasks run in parallel.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Glob and read `src/vscode-dts/**` through `gulp.src`, then read the existing registry to preserve line endings and detect unchanged output.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One source-tree stream and up to two registry reads per explicit run; one regeneration per debounced watch burst.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, the same gulp glob was read and the same registry comparison/read occurred. The refactor replaces a stream filter/map with a path collection and shared pure generator without adding boundary calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to produce or confirm the registry before the explicit generation task completes; in watch mode it is off the type-check critical path because watcher tasks run in parallel.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write `src/vs/platform/extensions/common/extensionsApiProposals.ts` only when generated contents differ.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero writes for unchanged output, one write for stale or missing output.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The pre-diff generator emitted the same single output only when contents changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Same conditional output behavior as before; no added write amplification.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All entries under `src/vscode-dts`, with effective proposal generation cardinality deduplicated by proposal name. The new path array temporarily includes non-proposal entries, but this directory is small and the array is released after each stream flush.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each gulp source stream and generator flush is serial. Watch events are coalesced by the existing `util.debounce(task)` and regeneration remains parallel with the other top-level watch tasks.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No persistent generation cache was added or removed. Gulp/watch and the OS may serve warm metadata/pages; unchanged output is still detected by comparing the generated string with the existing registry and skips the write.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the before/after diff that source discovery, debounce, registry comparison, and conditional write behavior remain equivalent. The only retained-state increase is a small temporary array of all source paths rather than proposal map entries.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact directory entry count beyond the roughly 135 proposals is not enumerated, but repository layout and the generated registry show the collection is bounded. No changed boundary multiplicity depends on that uncertainty.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The refactor does not increase filesystem-call frequency, watch scheduling, or output writes; temporary path retention is bounded to one stream flush.

Scenarios.Scenario: Focused build-script tests for registry validation and core-ci sequencing
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new tests create small temporary repositories, run synchronous validation, and snapshot fixtures before/after assertions. This work is on the test invocation path only and does not affect editor startup or runtime.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/remove temporary fixtures and recursively stat/read their contents for read-only assertions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A fixed small fixture per test and several snapshots in sequencing/read-only cases; no repository-sized recursive snapshot except the validation itself scans only `src/vscode-dts`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These focused registry tests and their temporary filesystem operations did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds bounded test-suite latency only when build-script tests are run.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Full downstream core-ci subprocesses are replaced by instrumentation in sequencing tests; only the real proposal check executes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero real type-check/transpile/bundle subprocesses from these tests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Avoids expensive production build work while preserving task-order assertions.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed test matrix with fixtures containing two proposal declarations, two ignored files, one registry, and a handful of directories. Recursive snapshots scale only with each tiny fixture.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Node test cases in these suites use synchronous fixture I/O around awaited task tests; process-wide `chdir` use is serialized by the runner behavior exercised here. No unbounded task or subprocess fan-out is introduced by the tests.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each test uses a fresh temporary directory, so fixture metadata is initially cold; snapshots reread the same tiny files and may benefit from OS cache. Fixtures are removed in test cleanup, so no retained cache or artifact growth remains.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that test-only filesystem work is bounded by fixed fixtures and cleanup; the test instrumentation explicitly suppresses full build consumers.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runner-wide test frequency is not quantified, but per-test fixture size and operation count are fixed and small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added test overhead is bounded, cleans up all temporary state, and avoids spawning the expensive build consumers.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and all diff pages. Traced CI validation, developer generation/watch, and test scenarios through filesystem and subprocess boundaries. The only new production cost is a once-per-core-ci synchronous scan/read of a modest proposal corpus before a much larger build; no high-confidence material performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
